target_customer: Shoppers in countries with limited access to goods (early users mostly Bangladesh, then China) and travelers willing to carry items for a fee
problem: Buying products from overseas is expensive or impossible to ship; Backpack matches shoppers with travelers who buy and carry items, with payment held in escrow.
business_model: Marketplace take rate / fee on peer-to-peer delivery

founders.name: Fahim Aziz
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as founder and CEO; no further bio on YC page.

founders.name: Sakib Sauro
founders.background_notes: Named only in a Substack opinion piece; not on the YC page, unverified.

competitors.name: PiggyBee
competitors.what: Matches senders with travelers and commuters who carry items, with MoneySafe escrow
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2012; couriers often paid with trade rather than cash

competitors.name: Shipizy
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2012, still in beta; users from 50 countries

technical_complexity.rationale: A two-sided web marketplace with escrow payments and trip matching; the hard parts are trust, payments in many countries and fraud, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace liquidity could create local network effects, but peers existed since 2012 and trust and escrow features were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing startups kept operating through 2015; no incumbent acquisition or copy of Backpack found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Aug 2014) reported about 70,000 visits from 86 countries in the first week, 15% weekly growth and over two-thirds of requests fulfilled, concentrated in Bangladesh. Company-reported.

branding.domain_note: Operated at backpackbang.com, not the plain backpack.com; the YC directory lists that domain.

brand_strength.rationale: Common word that suggests travel, but generic: the name collides with 37signals' Backpack product and other Backpack brands in search; no community or press on the brand beyond launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: Backpack launched in February 2014, drew early traction from Bangladeshi shoppers and joined YC in Summer 2014 with about $120K. No later round, customer data or shutdown notice was found. An opinion Substack says traffic fell after 2019, but that is not corroborated, so the outcome stays uncertain.
notes: The $120K figure is from a headline seen in search results (Xconomy, page fetch failed) and Bouncewatch; it matches YC's 2014 standard deal so it is recorded as 'other', not a priced seed. A Village listing names Khosla and Matrix as backers, and PitchBook (via Substack) names Inflection Ventures; neither is verified. Directory status is Active but the website's current state could not be verified (DNS and search found nothing). The competitor list uses a 2015-03 roundup (updated 2018), seven months after the batch; Grabr appears in 2015-16 coverage only and is excluded. Name origin not stated.
